prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Generate one high-fidelity Birdcar operational consulting WEBSITE HOMEPAGE screenshot, 1536 by 1024 landscape, edge-to-edge actual website with no browser frame, no device, no photographed paper or mockup scene. This is an unapproved direction-decision comp.

REFERENCE ROLES: Image 1 /tmp/birdcar-alkaline-specimen.png supplies the EXACT TYPE IDENTITY ONLY: bold, forward-slanting, connected Alkaline script with the distinctive broad capital B and thick rounded connected lowercase. Recreate this lettering voice for the Birdcar logo and display headline. Its white canvas and sample copy are not layout or content instructions. Image 2 /tmp/birdcar-bebop-hero.webp supplies ONLY visual grammar and finish: mustard fields, asymmetric hard-cut teal bars, brick-red panels, warm cream, black silhouette cut paper, subtle print grain. Do not carry over any subject, copy, logo, grotesk headline type, music, jazz, anime, episodes, players, instruments, concerts, media cards, or entertainment navigation from image 2. This is a capable operational partner for established service businesses.

PAGE STRUCTURE, IN ORDER:
1. A shallow, readable navigation header on warm cream, Birdcar in Alkaline script at left, ordinary Barlow navigation links on the right: "How it works", "Selected work", "Contact". Keep this UI precise and usable.
2. Main hero below: a slim cream left index rail, approximately 110 pixels wide, with three calm stacked labels "Understand", "Build", "Care". Rest is a broad mustard #E0B23C field taking the majority of the screen. The SINGLE dominant focal moment is enormous black ALKALINE CONNECTED SCRIPT headline, matching reference 1, reading exactly "Make room for better work." Set it in two or three expressive lines with intentional breathing room and clear reading order; lowercase letters visibly connect. No geometric sans-serif display. No condensed caps for headline. Supporting line is Barlow, modest and very readable: "Custom systems for service businesses with too much chasing, copying and remembering."
3. One secondary, clearly conceptual black cut-paper illustration in the hero's right region: a small team arranging a shared work board and connecting tasks around a worktable. Human working together with simple visible workflow objects, not a photograph of a customer, not office clipart, no instruments. It must be much quieter and smaller than the hero headline. A hard asymmetric teal #146B6E band gives the region movement, but must never obscure text.
4. A hard-cut brick #B23A2E assessment panel underneath the hero, with ample warm-cream space around copy and an unmistakable rectangular cream button. Main panel text in readable ALKALINE SCRIPT at a smaller scale than hero: "Start with a free assessment." Barlow supporting text: "A conversation. A practical report. Yours to keep." Button in Barlow: "Book a free assessment". This is visibly the primary action, clean rectangular web control, not a decorative label.
5. At the bottom, show the start of a calm cream selected-work continuation, enough to prove this is a scrolling website. Two quiet project summaries, not flashy cards: "DataDash — Craft & Communicate" with body "A client-facing reporting platform built around the agency’s work." and "Workshops — GHX" with body "Practical team training grounded in real workflows." A small Barlow section label "Selected work" is fine. No fake metrics, client quotes, testimonials, screenshots, timelines, revenue, or claims.

VISUAL SYSTEM: mustard #E0B23C dominant, teal #146B6E hard asymmetric bars, brick #B23A2E secondary panels, warm cream #F1E6CF and near-black #0E0E0E. Crisp, confident page hierarchy with angular panels and very subtle tactile printed grain. Exact script voice from image 1 for Birdcar and all display typography; Barlow for supporting copy, navigation, index labels, project summaries, buttons. Energetic asymmetry in the large hero and panel edges, calm alignment and readable density in the supporting regions. One focal moment, not multiple competing poster titles. No browser chrome, no watermark, no option labels, no annotations. All specified UI copy correctly spelled and legible. This must unmistakably read as a useful business website with a clear first purchase, not an entertainment poster.
copyStatus: Predates the explicit first-person voice requirement; supporting copy and the implication of team imagery must be addressed before build approval.
